output.title: Spot free-tier limits before they break a workflow
output.body:
If you run a small business and use a free-tier tool, one useful workflow decision is simple: do you know when it is about to stop being free?

That could be a SaaS plan, an API, an email tool, or any service that quietly turns a convenience into a bill or a block. The question is not whether the tool is useful. The question is whether you know its quota and check usage before the limit is hit.

If you do not, you are leaving the timing to the vendor. That is rarely the best control surface.

A practical next step is to pick one tool in your stack and write down three things: the free limit, where usage is visible, and what reminder will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For others, a vendor cost-alert email is better. Keep it boring. Boring is good here.

Why it matters: an unexpected limit can interrupt a workflow or force an unplanned upgrade while you are still deciding whether the process is worth automating. Early spotting does not make that decision for you, but it keeps it human and deliberate.

If you want a clean test, start with one tool and one check.
